//buildCommand: THE TEST SUITE IS THE DEPLOY GATE.
Pushing to main deploys production through Vercel's git integration,
which does NOT go through `npm run deploy`. .github/workflows/check.yml
runs the same suite on every push, but it runs ALONGSIDE the deploy, not
before it — so a red build shipped anyway and the workflow only made the
failure visible afterwards. check.yml's own header names that problem;
running on push does not close it.
Setting buildCommand makes the deploy itself fail when the suite fails,
so production keeps serving the last good deployment instead of taking
the broken one. Output is unaffected: outputDirectory stays unset, and
Vercel's own placeholder documents the behaviour as 'public if it exists,
or .' — this repo has no public/, so the root is served exactly as before.
COST: a genuinely failing test now blocks a deploy. That is the point,
and it is the honest trade — the suite is deterministic and runs with no
network and no secrets (check.yml verified that under `env -i`), so a
failure here means the code is broken, not that the runner had a bad day.
